# Bet from iMessage — Messages App Extension

WagerPals ships a native **iMessage app extension** so you can create a bet, send it into a
thread, and let everyone take a side from inside Messages. The bubble is a live object: as
people pick sides it **updates in place** rather than piling up new bubbles.

Everything about the extension is generated from committed sources by an Expo config plugin.
**`mobile/ios/` is disposable** — it is gitignored and regenerated by `expo prebuild`. Never
hand-edit it; if something needs to change in the Xcode project, change the plugin.

---

## 1. Identifiers

| Thing | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Apple Team ID | `3C4383262W` |
| App bundle id | `com.wagerpals.app` |
| **Extension bundle id** | `com.wagerpals.app.messages` |
| App Group | `group.com.wagerpals.app` |
| Keychain access group | `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.wagerpals.shared` → `3C4383262W.com.wagerpals.shared` |
| Keychain service | `wagerpals` |
| App Store ID | `6754625373` |
| Xcode target / scheme | `WagerPalsMessages` |

An iMessage extension embedded in an app **must** have a bundle id that is the app's bundle id
plus one more component. `com.wagerpals.app.messages` satisfies that; anything else will be
rejected at embed time.

These live in exactly two places: the plugin props in `mobile/app.json` and the constants at the
top of `mobile/plugins/imessage-extension/withIMessageExtension.js`. Change them there, nowhere
else.

---

## 2. Apple Developer portal setup (one time)

Do this before the first device build. Simulator builds need none of it.

### 2.1 App Group

1. <https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/identifiers/list/applicationGroup>
2. **+** → *App Groups* → Description `WagerPals Shared`, Identifier `group.com.wagerpals.app`.

### 2.2 Keychain sharing group

Keychain access groups are **not** registered separately — they are just a string in the
entitlements, prefixed at build time by your team id. Nothing to create in the portal. The only
requirement is that both targets carry the identical `keychain-access-groups` entry, which the
plugin guarantees.

### 2.3 App IDs

You need **two** App IDs.

1. <https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/identifiers/list/bundleId>
2. The main app `com.wagerpals.app` should already exist. Edit it and make sure these
   capabilities are ON:
   - **App Groups** → select `group.com.wagerpals.app`
   - **Associated Domains**
   - **Push Notifications**
3. **+** → *App IDs* → *App* → Description `WagerPals Messages`, explicit Bundle ID
   `com.wagerpals.app.messages`. Enable:
   - **App Groups** → select `group.com.wagerpals.app`

   Do **not** enable Associated Domains or Push on the extension — it needs neither.

### 2.4 Provisioning profiles

With Xcode's automatic signing (which the plugin configures: `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`,
`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = 3C4383262W`), Xcode creates and refreshes both profiles for you the first
time you build to a device. You need one profile **per target** — a single profile cannot cover
both the app and the extension.

If you sign manually, or you are building on CI with `credentialsSource: remote`, create:

| Profile | App ID | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WagerPals Development` | `com.wagerpals.app` | iOS App Development |
| `WagerPals Messages Development` | `com.wagerpals.app.messages` | iOS App Development |
| `WagerPals Distribution` | `com.wagerpals.app` | App Store |
| `WagerPals Messages Distribution` | `com.wagerpals.app.messages` | App Store |

For EAS: `eas credentials` → iOS → select the extension's bundle id when prompted. EAS will
generate the second profile; a build that only has the app's profile fails at the *Embed
Foundation Extensions* step with a signing error naming the appex.

### 2.5 App Store Connect

The extension is **not** a separate App Store Connect record — it ships inside the WagerPals app
(`6754625373`) and is not separately purchasable.

There is one thing you must supply: an **iMessage App Icon**. It is a distinct asset from the app
icon, with its own aspect ratios (the Messages app drawer is landscape).

The plugin currently *generates* a valid but **imageless** `iMessage App Icon.stickersiconset`
inside `withIMessageExtension.js` (see `materializeExtensionFiles`) and sets
`ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME = "iMessage App Icon"` on the extension target. It compiles
as-is — the missing art never blocks a build, it only blocks App Store validation.

To add real art, edit the plugin so it copies PNGs from a committed source directory into the
generated `.stickersiconset` and writes their filenames into that `Contents.json`. **Do not just
drag images into `ios/WagerPalsMessages/Assets.xcassets` in Xcode** — `ios/` is regenerated by
`expo prebuild --clean` and your icons would vanish. Everything must come from the plugin.

Sizes Apple requires for a Messages app icon:

| Purpose | Size (px) |
| --- | --- |
| iPhone messages app store | 1024×768 |
| Messages iPhone | 120×90, 180×135 |
| Messages iPad | 134×100, 148×110 |
| Messages iPad Pro | 167×125 |
| Messages Drawer iPhone | 300×218 |
| Messages Drawer iPad | 54×40, 81×60, 64×48, 96×72 |

Validation (`xcodebuild -exportArchive`, or upload) fails if the set is incomplete, so do this
before you cut a release build.

## 3. Entitlements

Both targets get the same two entitlements. The plugin writes them; this is what the result
looks like.

**Main app** (`ios/WagerPals/WagerPals.entitlements`, generated):

```xml
<key>com.apple.security.application-groups</key>
<array><string>group.com.wagerpals.app</string></array>
<key>keychain-access-groups</key>
<array><string>$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.wagerpals.shared</string></array>
<key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key>
<array><string>applinks:wagerpals.io</string>…</array>
```

**Extension** (`ios/WagerPalsMessages/WagerPalsMessages.entitlements`, generated):

```xml
<key>com.apple.security.application-groups</key>
<array><string>group.com.wagerpals.app</string></array>
<key>keychain-access-groups</key>
<array><string>$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.wagerpals.shared</string></array>
```

`$(AppIdentifierPrefix)` is expanded by the build system to `3C4383262W.`. It is **only**
expanded in entitlements — never in `Info.plist`. That is why the plugin writes the literal
`3C4383262W.com.wagerpals.shared` into the extension's `Info.plist` key `WPKeychainAccessGroup`,
which is what the Swift code actually reads at runtime.

---

## 4. How session sharing works

The extension does **not** have its own sign-in. It reads the session the main app already holds.

```
main app (JS)                              extension (Swift)
─────────────                              ─────────────────
expo-secure-store                          Security.framework
  keychainService: "wagerpals"      ─────►   kSecAttrService: "wagerpals:no-auth"
  accessGroup:     "<team>.com.wagerpals.shared"
                                             kSecAttrAccessGroup: "<team>.com.wagerpals.shared"
  keys: accessToken, refreshToken,           kSecAttrAccount:     Data(key.utf8)
        user, sharedSession
```

Two details that are easy to get wrong and silently break everything:

- **`expo-secure-store` appends `:no-auth` to the service name** when `requireAuthentication` is
  false (the default). The stored item's `kSecAttrService` is therefore `wagerpals:no-auth`, not
  `wagerpals`. The Swift reader tries `:no-auth` first, then the bare name, then `:auth`.
- **`kSecAttrAccount` is the UTF-8 `Data` of the key, not a `String`.** Querying with a String
  matches nothing.

Items are written with `kSecAttrAccessible = AfterFirstUnlock` so the extension can read them
when Messages is opened on a locked-then-unlocked device.

Because this changes where tokens live, `mobile/src/services/shared-session.ts` runs a one-time
migration on app start: it reads any token at the legacy location (service `app`, no access
group), copies it to the shared group, and only then deletes the legacy copy. Without that, this
change would silently sign out every existing user.

Signing out of the app clears the shared keychain items too, so the extension loses access at
the same moment.

The **App Group** container is used by the extension for its own cache — the last group you
posted into and the cached group list — so the compact view renders instantly instead of showing
a spinner on every keystroke. The main app does not currently read or write it.

---

## 5. Server endpoints

| Route | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/imessage/session` | **required** | Signed-in user, their groups, and each group's active members |
| `POST /api/imessage/bets` | **required** | Create a bet from the extension |
| `POST /api/imessage/bets/side` | **required** | Take a side inline |
| `GET /api/events/preview?id=&t=` | public | Minimal state for rendering the bubble / invite page |

Every write requires a real Stack Auth session resolved by `lib/auth.ts`; the caller's identity
always comes from the session, never from the request body. User rows are created only through
`lib/sync-user.ts`, and cash bets only through `lib/payments.ts`.

`GET /api/imessage/session` returns each group's **active** members (id + username only), which
is what populates the expanded compose sheet's "This bet is about…" subject picker. A pending
join request is not a member and is not taggable. The server re-validates `subject_user_id`
against that same rule on `POST /api/imessage/bets` and returns 400 if it does not hold, so the
client-side filtering is convenience, not the security boundary.

### The share token

`GET /api/events/preview` is public, so it deliberately returns **no** usernames, no per-user
bets, no group, no description, and never `subject_user_id` / `notify_subject` — leaking either
would defeat a "quiet" bet about someone.

Money totals and the right for a **non-member** to take a side are gated on a **share token**: an
HMAC-SHA256 of the event id, keyed by `IMESSAGE_SHARE_SECRET`, carried in the message bubble.
Holding it proves you actually received the iMessage, and it is what turns receiving a bubble
into an invitation to that bet's group.

```bash
# .env.local  — required for iMessage sharing to grant access to non-members
IMESSAGE_SHARE_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
```

If the variable is unset the app still works: `createShareToken` returns `null`,
`verifyShareToken` always returns `false`, and the extension degrades to "you must already be a
member of the group". It never falls back to a default secret — a predictable token would be
forgeable.

### Verifying the server side without a database

`npm run verify:imessage` drives the **real** route handlers against in-memory fakes — no
database, no network, no side effects — and exits non-zero on any failure, so it works as a CI
gate. It covers the authorization rules (401s write nothing; identity always comes from the
session, never the body; share-token access control) and, most importantly, asserts that the
public preview never leaks a username, bet note, description, `group_id`, `subject_user_id` or
`notify_subject`, by seeding sentinel values and scanning the serialized response.

132 checks, all passing. The suite is proven load-bearing by mutation testing: making `buildEventPreview` emit `subject_user_id`/`description` makes it exit 1 naming exactly those keys. Extend it whenever you add a field to the preview payload.

> `npm run build` needs Stack Auth env vars present (`NEXT_PUBLIC_STACK_PROJECT_ID` and friends)
> because `app/api/auth/mobile-session` constructs the Stack client at module scope. That is a
> pre-existing repo-wide requirement, unrelated to the extension — but it means a bare checkout
> with no `.env.local` fails at "Collecting page data". Copy `.env.local.example` first.

---

## 6. Universal links

`app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts` serves the association file for
`wagerpals.io`. It must be served over HTTPS, as `application/json`, with **no** `.json`
extension and **no** redirect. Both app IDs are listed:

```
3C4383262W.com.wagerpals.app
3C4383262W.com.wagerpals.app.messages
```

`/invite`, `/events/*` and `/groups/*` are claimed; `/api/*`, `/handler/*` and `/.well-known/*`
are explicitly excluded so API calls are never swallowed by the app.

The flow for a recipient:

- **Has the app** → tapping the bubble opens the extension; "Open in WagerPals" fires the
  universal link and iOS hands it to the installed app, landing on that bet.
- **Does not have the app** → the same URL opens `https://wagerpals.io/invite?e=…` in Safari,
  which previews richly (OpenGraph) and offers `https://apps.apple.com/app/id6754625373`. After
  installing, the same link opens the app directly on that bet.

Verify a change with:

```bash
curl -sI https://wagerpals.io/.well-known/apple-app-site-association   # 200, application/json, no redirect
npx --yes app-site-association-validator wagerpals.io                  # optional third-party check
```

Apple caches the file through its CDN; after changing it, delete and reinstall the app on the
test device (or use a development build, which fetches directly) or the old file will stick.

---

## 7. Build and test

### Prerequisites

```bash
node -v          # 20+
xcodebuild -version
pod --version    # CocoaPods
```

### Generate the native project

```bash
cd mobile
npm install
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://wagerpals.io npx expo prebuild --platform ios --clean
```

`--clean` deletes `ios/` and rebuilds it from scratch. That is the point: if the extension only
exists because someone once added it in Xcode, `--clean` destroys it. Run `--clean` whenever you
touch the plugin, and treat "the target survived a clean prebuild" as the acceptance test.

Afterwards you should see:

```
ios/WagerPalsMessages/
├── *.swift                       (copied from mobile/plugins/imessage-extension/swift/)
├── Info.plist                    (NSExtensionPointIdentifier = com.apple.message-payload-provider)
├── WagerPalsMessages.entitlements
└── Assets.xcassets/
ios/WagerPals.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/WagerPalsMessages.xcscheme
```

### Build the extension for the simulator

The extension itself has **no CocoaPods dependencies**, so you can compile it straight from the
`.xcodeproj` without running `pod install` first. This is the fastest way to check that a Swift
change still builds, and it is the exact command used to verify this feature:

```bash
cd mobile
xcodebuild \
  -project ios/WagerPals.xcodeproj \
  -scheme WagerPalsMessages \
  -sdk iphonesimulator \
  -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  build
# => ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
```

`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` is correct for the simulator and lets the build run without any
provisioning profile. For a device build, drop it and let automatic signing take over.

To build the whole app (which embeds the extension) you DO need the pods and the workspace —
`ios/WagerPals.xcworkspace` only exists after `pod install`, and `expo prebuild --no-install`
deliberately skips it:

```bash
cd mobile/ios && pod install
xcodebuild -workspace WagerPals.xcworkspace -scheme WagerPals \
  -sdk iphonesimulator -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16' build
```

Confirm the built extension carries the right identity and configuration:

```bash
APPEX=$(find ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData -name WagerPalsMessages.appex | head -1)
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleIdentifier' "$APPEX/Info.plist"
# => com.wagerpals.app.messages
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :NSExtension:NSExtensionPointIdentifier' "$APPEX/Info.plist"
# => com.apple.message-payload-provider
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :WPKeychainAccessGroup' "$APPEX/Info.plist"
# => 3C4383262W.com.wagerpals.shared   <- must match what shared-session.ts writes
```

That last value is the one to check first whenever the extension claims you are signed out.

### Run it in the simulator

```bash
cd mobile
npx expo run:ios
```

Then, in the simulator:

1. Open **Messages** and start a conversation (the simulator has a built-in dummy thread; on a
   fresh simulator, type any number into *To:*).
2. Tap the **App Store icon (Ⓐ)** beside the text field → the app drawer opens.
3. Tap the **`...` / grid** button → **Edit** → enable **WagerPals** if it is not visible.
4. Select WagerPals. You get the **compact** presentation.

> The extension only appears if the containing app is installed on that simulator. If it is
> missing, the appex did not get embedded — check the *Embed Foundation Extensions* build phase
> in the generated project.

### What to check

| Check | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Compact view, signed in | Your groups appear in the picker; title + two sides + deadline fit without scrolling |
| Compact view, signed out | "Open WagerPals to sign in" — no second sign-in flow inside Messages |
| Expanded compose | Payment type, stake, subject tag and the notify-subject toggle are all present |
| Send | A bubble appears; `GET /api/events?id=<id>` shows the event really exists server-side |
| Recipient taps the bubble | Extension opens on that bet showing live counts |
| Take a side | The **same** bubble updates — no second bubble is inserted |
| Reopen an old bubble | Counts reflect current server state, not the state at send time |
| "Open in WagerPals" | Opens the app on that event; with the app deleted, Safari shows `/invite` |

### Debugging

The extension is a separate process, so `npx expo run:ios` logs will not show it.

```bash
# Attach Console to the extension
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'process == "WagerPalsMessages"' --level debug
```

Or in Xcode: **Debug → Attach to Process by PID or Name…** → `WagerPalsMessages`.

Common failures:

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| Extension missing from the drawer | appex not embedded, or bundle id is not `<app id>.messages` |
| Always shows signed-out | Keychain group mismatch — compare the app's entitlement with `WPKeychainAccessGroup` in the extension's `Info.plist` |
| Every side-take spawns a new bubble | A fresh `MSSession()` was used instead of `conversation.selectedMessage?.session` |
| 403 taking a side | `IMESSAGE_SHARE_SECRET` unset (token unverifiable) and the taker is not a group member |
| Universal link opens Safari on a device that has the app | AASA cached; reinstall the app, or check for a redirect on the `.well-known` URL |

---

## 8. Where the code lives

```
mobile/plugins/imessage-extension/
├── withIMessageExtension.js     ← the ONLY thing that edits the Xcode project
└── swift/
    ├── WagerConfig.swift        ← reads WP* keys out of Info.plist
    ├── WagerModels.swift        ← Codable mirrors of the server JSON
    ├── WagerSession.swift       ← shared-keychain read + App Group cache
    ├── WagerAPI.swift           ← async URLSession client
    ├── WagerMessageComposer.swift ← MSMessage encode/decode + bubble image
    ├── MessagesViewController.swift
    ├── CompactWagerView.swift
    ├── ComposeWagerView.swift
    └── TakeSideView.swift

mobile/src/services/shared-session.ts   ← publishes the session into the shared keychain
app/api/imessage/**                     ← server endpoints
app/api/events/preview/route.ts         ← public bubble/invite state
app/invite/page.tsx                     ← logged-out landing page with OpenGraph
lib/imessage-share.ts                   ← share-token HMAC
```

Every `.swift` file in `swift/` is picked up automatically at prebuild time — adding a file
needs no plugin change.
